title: Safety gates for multi-model orchestration — scratchpad (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for defining safety gates, instrumentation, and playbook steps specific to multi-model orchestration rollouts (e.g., routing different model families/variants per traffic slice, ensemble/reranker handoffs, and conditional fallbacks). Focus is operational: how to safely expose new model variants while preserving availability, latency targets, cost envelopes, and quality.

Audience: product owners, rollout stewards, SRE, serving-runtime, applied-ml, solutions engineering.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Canary and A/B design where the route is model-dependent (not just feature flag).
- Multi-variant experiments (float vs quantized, small vs large model, reranker on/off).
- Observability hooks required to detect model-specific drift or regressions.
- Automated vs manual gates and escalation path.

Non-goals:
- Full statistical primer on A/B math (see stats-team playbook).
- Detailed infra runbook for provisioning GPUs (handled by infra team).

High-level goals for a safe multi-model rollout:
- Catch behavioral regressions early (quality drop, hallucination patterns).
- Preserve latency SLOs and keep cost within budgeted per-request unit economics.
- Provide deterministic, auditable rollback paths per cohort/route.
- Ensure consistent user experience despite model heterogeneity.

Key failure modes we need to guard for (notes):
- Tokenization/normalization mismatch causing truncated outputs or mismatched alt text.
- Reranker/ensemble mismatch: downstream component assumes a distribution that the new model breaks.
- KV-cache incompatibility across model families causing cold-slow latency spikes.
- Undetected semantic regressions that don't show up in simple BLEU-like metrics.
- Cost spikes due to an unintended routing loop or larger model being selected for bulk traffic.

Proposed safety gates (ordered):
1) Preflight (pre-canary)
   - Model card + checklist: known failure modes, dataset provenance, tokenizer, max-seq heuristics.
   - Offline eval against canonical prompt suite (golden prompts): P95 quality metrics, regression delta < X% (TBD).
   - Throughput smoke test on staging with simulated traffic (latency p95, memory, OOM checks).
   - Approval from applied-ml + serving-runtime.

2) Canary activation (micro-slices)
   - Microcohort selection: prefer stable internal traffic or invited testers.
   - Start at 0.5% of the selected slice (or fixed qps floor) for 6–12 hours.
   - Observability checklist running continuously: telemetry below.
   - If any hard-failure (see hard thresholds) -> immediate auto-fallback to baseline.

3) Progressive ramp (guarded)
   - Ramp steps: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% (example; adjust per product).
   - Hold windows at each step (6–24 hours depending on metric sensitivity).
   - At each hold evaluate both safety and business metrics.

4) Post-activation monitoring and bake period
   - Longer term drift checks (7-day rolling) and sampling for human review.

Observability (what we measure) — must be model-aware:
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 for route+model, cold vs warm (cache hit vs miss).
- Error rates: HTTP 5xx, inference failures, timeouts.
- Resource signals: GPU memory pressure, encoder/decoder stall metrics, OOM frequency.
- Quality: evaluation-set score deltas (nlg-metric, preferred-quality-metric), classification/regression accuracy for tasks with ground-truth.
- Behavioral signals: hallucination proxy (contradiction detection), repetition, user fallback rate (users hitting 'regenerate' or undo).
- Cost per request / per token: monitor burn-rate vs expected.
- Downstream impact: reranker score distribution shift, click-through delta, conversion delta (product metric dependent).

Suggested hard thresholds (examples, tune per-product):
- Latency P95 increases > 40% over baseline for the route+model -> rollback.
- Error rate increase (5xx + inference-exception) > 0.5 percentage points absolute -> rollback.
- Quality score regression on golden set > 5% relative -> hold & manual review.
- Cost per active user increases > 25% without measurable quality gain -> pause ramp and cost-investigation.

Composite pass/fail rule: define a weighted score where higher-severity signals (serviceability) are top priority; if any top-tier threshold violated -> auto-fallback. Middle-tier issues trigger human-in-loop review.

A/B testing specifics when routing is model-based:
- Randomization: assign on user-id hash + route salt to ensure stability across repeated sessions.
- Exposure unit: choose user-level exposure (recommended) to avoid contamination when model stateful (chat history).
- Dedupe: ensure experiments respect dedup across devices if user_id is known.
- Sequential testing: apply sequential p-value correction or predefine stopping rules to avoid peeking.
- Bucketing rules must include a model-compatibility layer: if a user has features incompatible with new model variant, exclude or route to baseline.

Multi-model orchestration nuances (important):
- Tokenizer compatibility: enforce canonical token mapping or ensure route translates properly.
- KV cache affinity: if two model variants share cache keyspace, avoid routing split that would thrash cache (prefer sticky routing).
- Fallback mapping: ensure fallback model is compatible with downstream (e.g., if new model produces structured json, fallback must have same shape).
- Ensemble: if scoring model changes distribution, retrain downstream calibrator during canary window.
- Model lineage tagging: every inference must carry model-version, quantization, and kernel metadata for triage.

Instrumentation and sample capture:
- Capture N random examples per minute + all failed traces for first 24h of ramp.
- Flagged-sample queue for human review (ops + applied-ml).
- Golden prompt sweep nightly for first 7 days post full rollout.
- Annotated replay environment for reproducible reruns (include deterministic seeds).

Alerts and Pager integration (ops-friendly):
- Severity-1 alert: service-impacting (mass OOMs, 5xx spike > threshold, auto-fallback triggered) -> oncall page + product-steward notify.
- Severity-2 alert: quality regression on golden set exceeding warning threshold -> slack channel, product review.
- Include runbook links in alert payload and model metadata.

Escalation and rollback playbook (quick steps):
1) Confirm signal: look at model-tagged telemetry & sample captures.
2) If S1 -> trigger immediate routing rule to baseline with canary traffic mapping rollback API (automated).
3) Notify stakeholders (steward + ML owner + SRE).
4) Postmortem: short RCA within 24h, deeper root cause within 5 working days.
5) Remediation options: patch model, adjust tokenization, change routing, or retract feature.

Roles and responsibilities (proposed):
- Rollout steward (owner of activation): coordinates ramp, signs off holds.
- ML owner: accountable for model quality and fixes.
- Serving-runtime / SRE: responsible for latency/availability gates and rollback hooks.
- Product PM: owns downstream business metric evaluation and release decision.
- Observability lead: ensures dashboards and SLOs are configured pre-canary.

Operational checklist (quick):
- [ ] Model card + dataset provenance attached to model artifact.
- [ ] Offline golden-suite regression < threshold.
- [ ] Staging smoke passed (latency + memory).
- [ ] Dashboards: route+model time-series + sample capture visible.
- [ ] Alerts configured with runbook links.
- [ ] Stakeholders notified of ramp schedule and escalation path.
- [ ] Cost guardrail configured for auto-pause.

Example ramp timeline (concrete numbers for a SaaS chat route):
- T0 (00:00): 0.5% invited testers, 12h hold.
- T1 (12:00): 2% internal users, 12h hold.
- T2 (24:00): 10% random U.S. geo, 24h hold + quality sweep.
- T3 (48:00): 25% + run conversion metric test for 72h.
- T4 (120:00): 50% hold 72h.
- T5 (192:00): 100% if all gates green.

Open questions & TODOs (investigate before next iteration):
- What is the canonical golden-suite for reranker-driven flows? (Mateo to draft list)
- How to represent composite score weighting in the console UI so non-stat folks can interpret (Anika + Observability)
- Define cost-pause vs cost-rollback boundaries (need input from finance).
- Decide default microcohort size for models with stateful session histories.
- Integration test for tokenizer mismatch detection (can we detect automatically?).

Notes to self / friction points we've seen in past rolls:
- When we split routing by model_id only, downstream DB joins that expect certain text shape blow up. Need schema compatibility validation.
- Small traffic (0.5%) sometimes lacks statistical power to detect subtle quality regressions; supplement with targeted golden prompts.
- Auto-fallbacks must not cascade: ensure single-rollout flip doesn't trigger unrelated rollouts.

Reference quick links (local):
- Confluence: Model-Orchestration-Playbook
- Stats primer: "Sequential testing for product experiments"
- Infra PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/212

If you are reading this and want to help: add concrete metric thresholds for your product route — put numbers under the "hard thresholds" section and tag me.

---
Scratchpad end. This will be converted to a formal playbook after 1–2 iterations of field notes and an internal dry-run.
